Syed Mohammad Ali with Ahsanul Kabir ----- For the Petitioner. 
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury ----- For the State.
parties:
Ruhul Amin ----- Petitioner
Vs.
State ----- Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammed Habibur Rahman J : This Rule was issued on 24-11-95 at the instance of the accused petitioner calling upon the Deputy Commissioner Chittagong to show cause why the order dated 10-11-85 passed by the Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Sessions Trial Case No. 103 of 1981 rejecting the petition of accused Ruhul Amin to release him on stopping the trial on 30th September, 1985 under the provision of section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 should not be set aside and the trial should not be stopped and the accused petitioner should not be released or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The case for the prosecution is that on 29-10-78 at 17-00 hours in village Jahanpur, PS Fatickchari accused petitioner Ruhul Amin shot from his gun and murdered Professor Abul Faiz. In this case the FIR was lodged on 30-10-78 in the FIR deceased Professor Abul Faiz's step-brother Serajul Islam falsely stated that accused Delwar Hossain killed his step-brother Professor Abul Faiz by gun shot. The Police after investigation submitted charge sheet on 11-1-79 against accused petitioner Ruhul Amin recommending discharge of accused Delwar Hossain and 21 others who were accordingly discharged on 15-1-79. On 9-3-81 accused Ruhul Amin surrendered before the Sub- Divisional Magistrate, Sadar (North), Chittagong in this case. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate allowed him to go on ad-interim bail directing him to appear before the Sessions Judge and sent the record to the Sessions Judge, Chittagong under the Law Reforms Ordinance. 1978. The accused petitioner did not appear before the Sessions Judge, Chittagong. On 10-3- 81 the; Sessions Judge, Chittagong passed the following order: 

 "Record received from SDO (North,) Chittagong as per Law Reforms Ordinance of 1978. Charge sheet submitted under section 302 BPC against accused Ruhul Amin. Cognizance be taken. Register as a Sessions Trial Case. Let the case be transferred to the learned 2nd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong for favour of disposal." 

 "In view of the Gazette Notification No. 52 dated 4-8-82 let the case be sent to the Special Martial Law Court No. 3 at Chittagong for favour of disposal. Note in the relevant Register." 

 It appears from the record of the Special Martial Law Court No.3 that the said Special Martial Law Court received the case record on 16-2-83 for trial as per Gazette Notification No. 52 dated 4-8-82. The accused petitioner remained absconding till 8-11-84 on which date he surrendered before the said Special Martial Law Court. He was allowed to go on bail. The Special Martial Law Court ceased to function from 16-1-85 as per CMLA's Secretariat Letter No. 6506/13/ML-2(A) dated 24-12-84. The Chairman of the Special Martial Law Court ordered on 26-1-85 to send the case to the Court of Sessions. The accused petitioner appeared before the Additional Sessions Judge-in-Charge on 27-1-85 and prayed for bail. His prayer for bail was rejected on 11-2-85. Thereafter the accused petitioner went on praying for bail and lastly on 28-2-85 he was released on bail. On 2- 5-85 the accused petitioner filed a petition for staying further proceedings of the present case till the hearing of Criminal Case No. 160 of 1979 in the Court of Upazilla Magistrate, Fatickchari. On 20-5-85 the complainant party filed a petition for cancelling the bail of the accused petitioner. Both the prayer of the accused for staying further proceedings of the present case and the prayer of the complainant party for cancellation of bail was fixed on several dates for hearing, but before the said petitions could be heard, the Sessions Judge withdrew the case on 9-9-85 to his own file. Before the Sessions Judge the accused petitioner filed a petition on 4-11-85 praying that in view of the provisions of section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 as amended by Ordinance No. XXIX of 1985 the accused petitioner is to be deemed to have been released on 30 September 1985 on stopping the trial. The learned Sessions Judge rejected the prayer holding that section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 applies to cases in which cognizance was taken on or after 21-8-82 (that is, the date of coming into force of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982) in view of the fact that in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 in the non-obstante clause specific mention of the newly inserted section 339C of Code of Criminal Procedure was made omitting to mention section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982, that the cognizance of the present offence having been taken on 10-3-81 by the Judge, the present case is covered by section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 which is directory and not mandatory and that since on 8-8-83 on which date Ordinance No XXXVII of 1983 came into force the present case was not pending before the Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge or Assistant Sessions Judge but was pending before the Special Martial Law Court, section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 has no manner of application in the present case, Thereafter the accused petitioner obtained this Rule. 

 4. Syed Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner submits that the present Sessions case became pending for trial in the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court from the date of receipt of the case record on 11-3-81 and since the case came back from the Martial Law Court again before the Sessions Judge, on 27-1-85, under the provision of Section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 which came into force on 8-8-83 the accused petitioner has acquired the right to be released on 30 September 1985 on stopping the trial as the trial was not concluded before 30 September 1985. 

 5. For clear understanding of section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 it is necessary to notice the fact that by Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 (read with Ordinance LX of 1982) section 339C was newly inserted for the first time in the Code of Criminal Procedure providing time limit for concluding trial of a case and also providing that if the trial cannot be concluded within the specified time or extended time, further proceedings in respect of the trial shall stand stopped and the accused person released. The law makers were aware of the pendency of a very large number of cases in which cognizance had already been taken before the coming into force of Ordinance No XXIV of 1982 on 21-8-82 and so for those pending cases it was specially provided in section 35(c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 as follows: 

 (c) any case, including an appeal, other than a case or appeal in respect of an offence under section 400 or section 401 of the Penal Code (Act XLV of 1960), which, immediately before the commencement of this Ordinance, was pending in any Court, including the Supreme Court, shall be disposed of within a period of three hundred and sixty days from the date of such commencement." 

 6. It is well-settled that a case becomes a pending case as soon as cognizance is taken by a competent Court. In the instant case after the submission of charge sheet on 11-1-79 and transmission of the case record from the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate to the Court of the Sessions the learned Sessions Judge took cognizance of the offence on 10-3-81. Therefore since 10-3-81 this was a pending case and as such the present case comes within the purview of section 35(c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 and does not come within the mischief of the newly inserted section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure which came into force on 21-8-82 by Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. Section 35(c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 provides that any case which was pending in the court on 21-8-82, that is on the date of coming into force of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 shall be disposed of within a period of 360 days from the date of comment cement of the Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982; but section 35(c) does not significantly provide that on the failure to dispose of the case within the said period the trial shall stand stopped and the accused persons shall stand released. Therefore, section 35(c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 is directly and not mandatory. It is well settled that changes in the adjective law or procedural law made in the statute have retrospective effect unless contrary intention is expressed in the statute or unless there be some good reason against taking such view. In the Book on Interpretation of Statutes by Maxwell, 9th Edition, Page 233 it has been observed. "The general principle, however, seems to be that alteration in procedure are retrospective, unless there be some reason against it'. This view follows from the decisions in the cases of James Gardner vs Edward A Lucas, (1878) 3 IA 582; Colonial Sugar Refining Co. vs Irving 1905 AC 369 Delhi Cloth and General Mills. Co. Ltd. vs Income-Tax Commissioner, Delhi, AIR 1927 PC 242. In the last mentioned case it has been observed by the Privy Council that provisions of a statute dealing merely with matters of procedure may have retrospective effect attributed of them unless that construction be textually inadmissible. In the present case the law makers by providing special provision for pending cases in section 35(c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 have made it apply clear that provisions of newly inserted section 339C which came into force on 21-8-82 shall not apply to cases which were pending on 21-8-82, that is, the cases in which cognizance had been taken by the competent Court before 21-9-82. 

 "(8) Special extension of time limit in certain cases. -Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the said Code, trial of any case pending, on the commencement of this Ordinance, before a Magistrate or a Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge or Assistant Sessions Judge shall continue and be concluded before the 30th September, 1985; and if such trial cannot be concluded before that date, further proceedings in respect of the trial shall stand stopped and the accused person released." 

 8. In the present case while narrating the facts of the case we have already shown that although the learned Sessions Judge received the case on 10-3-81 and took cognizance of the offence on that date but without securing the attendance of the accused petitioner he transferred the case to the Second Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong for disposal. We have also shown that when Ordinance No, XXXVII of 1983 came into force on 8-8-83, the trial of the present case could not commence as the case stood transferred to the Special Martial Law Court and as the accused petitioner was still absconding. So it cannot be said that when Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 came into force on 8-8-83 the trial of the present case was pending before a Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge or Assistant Sessions Judge, although it is true that since the cognizance had been taken on 10-3-81, the case was pending. The expression used in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 is "trial of any case pending on the commencement of this Ordinance." There is a significant and substantial difference between the expressions "a pending case" and "the trial of a case pending" (as used in said section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983): For a clear understanding of the matter as to when a trial can be said to commence it is useful to quote the following provisions of section 35(a) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. 

 (a) any case (other than an appeal) which, immediately before the commencement of this Ordinance, was pending in a Court of Session and is triable by a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class under the provisions of the said Code as amended by this Ordinance shall- 

 (i) if trial of such case has already commenced, be disposed of by that Court as if no such amendment had been made; 

 (ii) if trial of such case not already commenced. on such commencement, stand transferred for disposal to the Metropolitan Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class, as the case may be, having jurisdiction to try the case." 

 9. Although the term "trial" has now here been defined in the Code of Criminal Procedure, yet we get the clue from section 35 (a) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 itself that trial cannot be said to commence unless sub- stance of accusation is stated to the accused or a charge is framed against the accused and it is well settled that a trial ends when the accused is acquitted or convicted. A case becomes a pending case as soon as cognizance is taken by a competent Court, but the trial of a case cannot be said to be pending unless the trial has commenced and the trial cannot commence unless a charge is framed or substance of accusation is started to the accused. In the present Case since the charge could be not framed by the Additional Sessions Judge as the accused remained absconding and on the date of coming into force of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 the case on transfer or by Gazette Notification was pending in the Special Martial Law Court, it cannot be said that the trial of the case was pending before a Sessions Judge or an Additional Sessions Judge or an Assistant Sessions Judge when Ordinance No XXXVII of 1983 came into force on 8-80-83. So section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 has no manner of application in the present case. 

 10. Further, in Section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1981 instead of using the expression -Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force" or instead of using the expression "Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the Code of section 35(c) of Ordinance No XXIV of 1982" the law makers used the expression "Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the Code" and significantly omitted to include the time specified in section 35 (c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 in the non-obstante clause. Provisions of section 339C CrPC regarding stopping of trial and release of the accused persons apply only to cases cognizance of which, was taken on or after 21-8-82, that is the date of coming into force of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. There is no provision for stopping of trial and release of accused in respect of cases covered by section 35 (c) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982. The expressions "Notwithstanding the time specified in section 3399C of the said Code, "trial of any case pending on the commencement of this Ordinance", "shall continue" and marginal note "Special extension of time limit in certain cases" in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 sufficiently indicate that in spite of contrary provisions regarding time limit in section 339C CrPC the trial of cases pending on 8-8-83 coming within the mischief of section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure are to be concluded before 30 September 1985 failing which the trial shall stand stopped and the accused shall stand released and section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 does not include cases covered by section 35(C) of Ordinance No XXIV of 1982. In Halsbury's Laws of England, 3rd Edition, Vol. 36, page 402 it has been stated as follows: 

 In the case of Bangladesh vs Abdul Mannan, 29 DLR (SC) 17 it was observed: 

 11. In the present case in the non-obstinate clause in section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 the newly inserted section 339C has been expressly mentioned by using the expression "Notwithstanding the time specified in section 339C of the Code" and section 35(C) of Ordinance No. XXIV of 1982 regarding cases cognizance of which has already been taken by a competent Magistrate or Court of Sessions before 21-8-82 has been deliberately excluded, thereby making section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 only applicable to cases coming within the mischief of section 339C CrPC on 8-8-83 the date of coming into force of Ordinance No XXXVII of 1983 excluding the pending cases covered by section 35(C) of Ordinance No, XXIV of 1982. 

 12. Further, even if it were true that section 8 of Ordinance No XXXVII of 1983 would apply in respect of all cases pending for trial on 8-8-83 before a Magistrate or in the Court of Session, since the trial of the present case was not pending before the Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge or Assistant Sessions Judge on 8-8-83 but was pending before the Special Martial Law Court on that day; that is the day on which Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 care into force, section 8 of Ordinance No XXXVII of 1983 has no manner of application in the instant care and on that ground also the accused petitioner did not acquire any right to be released on 30 September 1985 by virtue of section 8 of Ordinance No. XXXVII of 1983 we, therefore, find that the learned Sessions Judge rightly rejected the prayer of the accused to be released on stopping the trial. 

 13. The Rule is accordingly discharged. The learned Session Judge, Chittagong is directed to conclude the trial of the case as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law on receipt of the lower Court record.
